text:
incident-bot: PAGER — P1 — Dedicated pool 'dedicated-acme-east-1' reports GPU capacity exhausted. 95 pending allocation requests, 0 GPUs available. Impact: AcmeCorp (enterprise VPC) inference jobs failing / timing out. Dashboard: https://internal.redwood/dashboard/pools/dedicated-acme-east-1 :rotating_light:

alex: on it. seeing the alert. queuing context, joining call.

jamie: joining. I'm pulling autoscaler state + recent events.

dave: oncall takeover if needed in 10. initial thought: autoscaler didn't burst. last change to pool scaling was a week ago (min=2, max=8, burst=0).

alex: confirming — Acme is on a dedicated single-tenant GPU pool pinned to east-1. They hit an unexpected traffic spike after a batch rollout. We have strict tenant isolation so other customers unaffected.

morgan: EM to Acme (cc: paola) — pls hold while we triage. We should prepare a short customer-facing line: "We're seeing resource saturation on your dedicated pool and are activating emergency scaling."

emma: tagging support stack. any ETA? customers are seeing 5xx and long tail latencies.

jamie: grabbing kube-level state:
```
$ kubectl get pods -n pool-dedicated-acme -o wide
NAME                                READY  STATUS   NODE
inference-acme-0                    1/1    Running  gpu-node-12
inference-acme-1                    0/1    Pending  <none>
inference-acme-2                    0/1    Pending  <none>
```
And scheduler events: "0/12 nodes available: Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu."

alex: nvidia-smi on gpu-node-12 shows all GPUs pinned by long-lived sessions:
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id | Volatile | Used-Memory |
|   0  A100-40GB    Enabled       ...        ...        38489 MiB |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
Looks like model cache + persistent workers consumed memory.

dave: autoscaler config (from infra):
```
pool: dedicated-acme-east-1
autoscaler:
  enabled: true
  min_replicas: 2
  max_replicas: 8
  surge_burst: 0   # burst disabled for single-tenant pool
  scale_cooldown: 120s
```
That explains no burst.

jamie: immediate mitigations we can attempt: enable temporary burst (surge_burst=4) to spin up additional nodes from reserved capacity, or provision emergency nodes (manual scale to 12). Both require org-ops approval for billing + infra ops involvement.

alex: which is faster? enabling burst or manual scale?

dave: enabling burst flips a flag to allow use of a shared emergency capacity group that has hot standby nodes; takes ~90s to attach and schedule. Manual scale (new instances) is ~5-8 minutes for provisioning and container startup.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook #7 invoked: "Dedicated pool exhaustion — steps: 1) check surge_burst flag; 2) if surge disabled, toggle to X, monitor; 3) if unavailable, escalate to infra-provisioning to allocate spot/ondemand GPUs; 4) prepare customer notice."

alex: I'm going to toggle burst to 4 now. Executing CLI: `infractl pools update --pool dedicated-acme-east-1 --set autoscaler.surge_burst=4 --actor alex`

jamie: seen the command. watching cluster events.

alex: infractl response: accepted. Request to attach hot-standby nodes queued.

(1m) jamie: new nodes coming up, scheduler bound pods to gpu-node-18,gpu-node-19.

(3m) dave: pods starting, but a few still pending due to CUDA driver mismatch on one standby. patching driver on gpu-node-19 now.

(6m) jamie: driver patched, pods scheduled. metrics showing pending backlog decreasing from 95 -> 12. Request latency dropping.

emma: customer update draft: "We're actively scaling your dedicated pool to handle the increased traffic. We expect service restoration within ~10 minutes. We're also investigating the root cause and will follow up with a post-incident summary." Approve?

paola: send that. also offer the option to increase reserved capacity if they expect sustained traffic. cc sales for billing note.

morgan: agreed. I'll send with marker about possible charge for emergency capacity.

(12m) alex: backlog cleared. current pending = 0. GPUs used ~86% across nodes. No errors in scheduler.

dave: follow-ups:
- recommend enabling a small non-zero burst for this pool permanently (e.g., surge_burst: 2)
- set alert to trigger earlier (queued > 20 instead of 50)
- add a customer-specific traffic spike playbook with Acme SEs

jamie: root-cause hypothesis: simultaneous canary rollout from Acme + large customer batch caused transient cache-warm workloads that pinned GPUs. Autoscaler min/max were too narrow and burst disabled prevented short-term absorb.

ops-runbook-bot: Action items assigned: enable_permanent_burst_proposal (owner: jamie), lower_queue_alert (owner: alex), Acme-incident-PR (owner: morgan).

morgan: composing post-incident: timeline, what we changed (burst toggle), customer impact (5-12 minutes degraded), and recommended preventive changes. I'll loop in account team for contract/comms.

emma: any risk to multi-tenant pools from this change?

dave: no — the change only allowed existing standby nodes reserved for enterprise emergencies to attach to this single-tenant pool. We validated isolation boundaries; no other customers' running jobs were rebalanced.

alex: handoff: dave taking follow-up for the rest of the shift. If anything regresses, page me and escalate to infra-provisioning.

dave: acknowledged. I'll run a quick post-mortem doc and link to this thread.

paola: I'll notify Acme account lead that we've restored and will provide a summary.

incident-bot: Incident resolved: P1 -> P2 (mitigated). Closing pager for now. :white_check_mark:

morgan: thanks team.

jamie: recommended immediate config PR: `pool: dedicated-acme-east-1: autoscaler.surge_burst: 2; alert.queue_threshold: 20` — I'll open it now.

alex: good. closing thread after doc link posted.

(30m) dave: postmortem draft: https://internal.docs/incidents/1865001234-acme-pool-exhaustion (will attach logs + timeline)."
